results.title: iPayX FX Audit on Microsoft Azure Foundry
results.snippet:
## How it works
1. Provision a Microsoft Azure Foundry agent.
2. Add iPayX as an MCP server using our endpoint URL.
3. Authenticate with your iPayX API key.
4. Your agent can now call `audit_fx_transaction` in any workflow.
## Setup snippet
```
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient
from azure.ai.projects.models import McpToolDefinition
project = AIProjectClient(...)
agent = project.agents.create_agent(
model="gpt-4",
name="FX Audit Assistant",
tools=[
McpToolDefinition(
server_url="https://hvujzsdwcoweirroubeh.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp-server",
server_label="ipayx-fx-audit",
auth={"type": "bearer", "token": "<YOUR_IPAYX_API_KEY>"}
)
]
)
```

### Powered by iPayX AI Engine
iPayX AI Engine reads bank statements, detects FX spreads, and returns structured JSON output. Every audit response includes a confidence score and spread benchmark.

{
"mcpServers": {
"ipayx-fx-audit": {
"url": "https://mcp.ipayx.ai/mcp",
"headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ipx_live_your_key" }
}
}
}

Here are three common ways to plug iPayX into your product.
### FX broker / multi-currency platform
Send each client FX conversion (CAD→USD, EUR→CAD, etc.) to the iPayX API and return a 0–10 FX score with estimated hidden costs.
### Corporate treasury
Feed your international payments (supplier invoices) into iPayX to compare bank rates vs mid-market and track margin impact.
### Accounting firm / fractional CFO
Use the API to audit your clients' FX conversions at year-end

### Universal bank coverage — anywhere Plaid does not reach
Plaid covers US and CA institutions. For any other region — or when a connection fails — iPayX accepts **any bank statement in PDF or CSV, worldwide** — no degraded experience for your prospects.
